result.title: PhaseGate: Phase-Aware CPU Retrieval Scheduling for On-Device LLMs on Unified Memory
result.comment: 11 pages, 3 figures. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on On-Device Intelligence: Foundation Models under Real-World Constraints
result.summary: On-device assistants run GPU-based LLM inference alongside CPU retrieval on unified-memory systems. Under a saturated local-retrieval workload, four concurrent retrieval workers raise 95th-percentile (p95) decode latency by 60-61% on two M4 systems, whereas prefill latency rises by only 5.7-6.9%. We study LLM phase as an admission signal for independent CPU retrieval under controlled LLM workloads. PHASEGATE calibrates separate concurrency limits for prefill and decode, selecting four and one on our base-M4 configuration. Under a backlogged queue, it achieves 2.0 times the aggregate retrieval throughput of the best tested feasible fixed policy, with both p95 LLM latency metrics within 1.25 times their no-retrieval baselines in all seven held-out runs. A phase-blind control, TimeGate, uses the same two limits on a calibration-derived schedule without observing LLM phase. It achieves similar retrieval throughput but violates the output-token latency limit in every run. M2 and M2 Pro Mac minis reproduce the policy ordering, while output-length sweeps show that the advantage narrows as decode occupies more of each request.

AI.brief_summary: PHASEGATE 将 LLM 的 prefill 与 decode 阶段作为 CPU 检索任务的准入信号，为两个阶段分别标定并发上限，在统一内存的端侧设备上以阶段感知调度换取检索吞吐，并与不观察阶段的 TimeGate 对照。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文把「prefill/decode 阶段」当作影响资源竞争的隐状态并据此做准入决策，可能与 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的调度与停止决策、按推理阶段分配外部获取预算有概念联系，可供核查；但其关注的是端侧吞吐与延迟，而非 latent 推理状态本身。
